narrativeReportMd:
# ExampleScenario R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`ExampleScenario` has high-impact local breaking changes. The resource identity is stable, but the R6 ballot remodels actors, instances, instance versions, operation labels, operation typing, workflow nesting, and internal referential integrity. Direct R4 JSON using the old element names will not validate as R6, and transformed data may still fail new R6 invariants.

## Scope
The assessment used the local R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions plus directly related local ValueSets and CodeSystems. Inherited base-resource changes, including `language` binding and extension-governance details, are excluded and should be handled by base artifact reports.

## Main migration themes
The dominant theme is a move from informal strings toward keyed, internally constrained scenario models: `actorId`, `resourceId`, `versionId`, `name`, and operation `number`/`name` are replaced by `key`, `title`, structured `Coding`, references to reusable actor definitions, and invariants that require keys to be unique and referenced consistently. R6 also supports richer examples through structure profiles and example content references that R4 cannot round-trip cleanly.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact findings are the actor remodel, instance remodel, instance-version/contained-instance remodel, operation remodel, workflow nesting change, and new R6 invariants. These affect validation, generated model classes, serializer/deserializer code, FHIRPath expressions, and migration transforms.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is needed for mapping old actor type `entity` to R6 `system`, deciding how to populate new required `title` fields when R4 optional names/descriptions are absent, deciding how to map operation `number` versus `title`, and resolving R6 key/reference integrity failures.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Many additions could have been introduced alongside deprecated R4 elements, but the R6 design appears to be a substantive cleanup that normalizes keys, display titles, formal actor definitions, structured operation coding, and internal references. That cleanup improves conformance but is not wire-compatible with R4.

## Follow-up analysis
Analyze `ActorDefinition`, the common base resource artifacts, and terminology expansions for actor type, instance type, operation codes, and jurisdiction before finalizing automated production transforms.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `ExampleScenario` keeps the same resource identity but has high-impact local R4-to-R6 breaking changes. Top concerns are renamed/removed actor and instance fields, structured operation and workflow changes, and new R6 invariants that reject previously valid loose scenarios. The main uncertainty is terminology expansion/rationale for the R6 binding changes.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should be treated as a model transformation, not a version-label update. Existing R4 data must be rewritten from `actorId`/`resourceId`/`versionId` fields into R6 `key` fields, display names must become required `title` fields, actor and instance type codes need terminology mapping, nested workflow content must move into step context, and transformed data must pass new uniqueness and reference-integrity invariants.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural and cardinality findings because they come directly from the local R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions. Confidence is medium for exact terminology impact and design justification because full terminology expansions, official diffs, and narrative rationale were not available in the local inputs.

findings.title: Actor identifier/name fields were replaced by key/title, with title now required

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, `ExampleScenario.actor.actorId` was mandatory and `ExampleScenario.actor.name` was optional. The actor display name was not required.

newState.summary: R6 actor uses `key` 1..1 and `title` 1..1, with optional `definition`.

semanticText.definition: A system or person who shares or receives an instance within the scenario.

newState.narrativeMd: In R6, the old `actorId` element is gone. `ExampleScenario.actor.key` is mandatory, and `ExampleScenario.actor.title` is also mandatory for rendering.

facts.note: Semantically replaced by the required `title` field.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `actorId` and `key` both identify actors for internal references. `name` and `title` both provide the rendering label, but R6 makes the label mandatory.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct wire-format and validation break. R4 instances containing `actorId` or `name` use element names that are not part of the R6 content model, while R6 requires `key` and `title`. Generated R4 classes, serializers, FHIRPath expressions, and templates that access `actor.actorId` or `actor.name` must be changed.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The main risk is loss or mis-association of actor identities in scenario documentation, not direct clinical decision support.

justification.inferredGoal: Normalize actors to key/title terminology and support stricter internal references.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `actorId` and `name` in the base model, clarify `actorId` as the actor key, add optional `definition`, and enforce uniqueness/reference rules against `actorId`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of stable actor keys, renderable labels, and resolvable operation participants is reasonable. The level of breakage is probably avoidable, however, because the same computable key/reference behavior could have been expressed over R4's mandatory `actorId` without rejecting existing instances, and the new display-title expectation could have been introduced as a warning, profile requirement, or optional field rather than a new required base element.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base R6 design could have retained `actorId` as the normative key field and retained `name` as the display label, with clearer definitions and new invariants for uniqueness and initiator/receiver references. `actor.definition` could still be added as optional R6 content. If R6 also accepted new `key`/`title` aliases, duplicate actor representations could accumulate; the cleaner alternative is to live with the R4 names while tightening their semantics.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 wire compatibility but leaves older, less consistent names and weakens any base guarantee that every actor has display title text.

evidence.quote: ID or acronym of the actor

examples.examplesMd: The fragments are illustrative and omit unrelated required or recommended content. The key point is that the old field names are no longer valid R6 children.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 replaces the actor identity and label shape. `actorId` becomes `key`, while optional `name` becomes mandatory `title`. Existing R4 scenarios can therefore fail R6 validation both because they contain unknown old elements and because some actors may not have a value that can safely populate the new required title.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: A strict R6 validator will reject `actor.actorId` and `actor.name` as unknown children and will require `actor.key` and `actor.title` on each actor. R6-to-R4 conversion can usually map `key` back to `actorId` and `title` back to `name`, but R6 actor metadata such as `definition` has no R4 equivalent.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Transform each R4 actor by copying `actorId` to `key`. Populate `title` from R4 `name` when present; otherwise choose a deterministic display label, often the old `actorId`, and flag the case for review. Update codegen models, serializers, FHIRPath expressions, diagrams, and templates to use `actor.key` and `actor.title`.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change could have been made less disruptive by retaining deprecated aliases, but R6 appears to favor a cleaner keyed model. A compatibility extension could preserve the original R4 name when a generated title is not semantically equivalent.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Review title population rules carefully: using an identifier as a display title may be acceptable for technical systems but not for human actors.

findings.title: Actor type binding changed from ExampleScenario person/entity to ActorDefinition person/system/collective/other

oldState.summary: R4 actor.type was mandatory code with required ValueSet examplescenario-actor-type.

binding.description: The type of actor - system or human.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The local R4 CodeSystem contains `person` and `entity`; no full expansion was needed for this simple CodeSystem-backed ValueSet.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 required each actor to carry `type`, with local codes `person` or `entity`.

newState.summary: R6 actor.type is optional, still required-bound when present, and uses ActorDefinition actor type codes.

binding.description: The type of actor - system or non-system.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The local R6 CodeSystem contains `person`, `system`, `collective`, and `other`. The R4 `entity` code appears semantically replaced by R6 `system`, but this is an inferred mapping.

constraints.human: actor SHALL have either a type or a definition but not both

newState.narrativeMd: R6 allows `actor.definition` instead of `actor.type`, and if `type` is present it must use the ActorDefinition actor type value set.

facts.note: R6 permits type omission only because `actor.definition` can be used instead.
Inferred semantic replacement based on displays/definitions; no ConceptMap was present.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The path is unchanged, but the value set and permitted code system changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 actors commonly used `type: entity` for systems. That code is not in the R6 required binding, so a direct copy is invalid. R6 actors that use `system`, `collective`, `other`, or `definition` need mapping decisions before they can be represented in R4.

justification.inferredGoal: Align ExampleScenario actors with the new ActorDefinition resource and a richer actor taxonomy.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep R4 `entity` in the R6 required binding as a deprecated alias for the system-like actor category while adding the new ActorDefinition-aligned codes.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Aligning ExampleScenario with ActorDefinition's richer taxonomy is a reasonable R6 goal. The hard break for R4 `entity` values appears probably avoidable because R6 could have allowed the old code as a deprecated alias while preferring `system` for new content. A ConceptMap alone would be migration guidance, not a backward-compatible base design; the base-design alternative is to include the old code in the allowed value set during transition.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking alternative is an R6 value set that includes `person`, the new `system`/`collective`/`other` codes, and the R4 `entity` code marked deprecated or equivalent to `system`. That preserves R4-valid instances and still lets R6 systems use the refined taxonomy. The tradeoff is some long-term terminology debt and possible variation between producers that continue to emit `entity` and producers that switch to `system`.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old coded instances with modest terminology clutter, but leaves a deprecated synonym that implementers must normalize over time.

evidence.detail: R4 actor type codes include `person` and `entity`.
R6 actor type codes include `person`, `system`, `collective`, and `other`.

examples.examplesMd: The R4 example also needs the structural actor rename from the separate actor finding. This finding focuses on the code binding change.

findings.narrativeMd: The actor type vocabulary changed. R4's system-like code was `entity`, while R6's system-like code is `system` in a different code system, and R6 adds non-R4 categories such as `collective` and `other`. The path name did not change, which makes this easy to miss in naive field-by-field migrations.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Because both bindings are required, a validator must reject codes outside the bound value set. R4 `entity` is therefore not a valid R6 `actor.type` code unless transformed. Conversely, R6 `collective`, `other`, and actors represented only by `actor.definition` cannot be represented faithfully in R4's mandatory two-code actor type model.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Use an explicit mapping table. A likely mapping is R4 `person` to R6 `person` and R4 `entity` to R6 `system`, but confirm with domain owners. For R6-to-R4, decide whether `system`, `collective`, and `other` collapse to R4 `entity`, whether actor definitions are dereferenced, or whether a cross-version extension is needed.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The value set change seems motivated by alignment with `ActorDefinition`. It could have been less breaking with a ConceptMap or deprecated code alias. Without that, systems must carry local migration logic.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: No local ConceptMap was found for actor type conversion; the `entity` to `system` mapping is inferred from displays and definitions.

findings.title: Instance declarations were remodeled from resourceId/resourceType/name to key/structureType/title

oldState.summary: R4 instance used `resourceId` 1..1, `resourceType` 1..1 code, optional `name`, and optional `description`.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 modeled scenario data as FHIR resources: each instance had a resource id and a required FHIR resource type code.

newState.summary: R6 instance uses `key` 1..1, `structureType` 1..1 Coding, required `title`, and optional structure metadata/content.

binding.description: The structure that defines the instance

newState.narrativeMd: R6 generalizes instances beyond FHIR resources. It requires an internal `key`, a `Coding` that names the data structure, and a display `title`; it may also carry structure version, profile, and example content references.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `resourceId` and `key` are both the internal instance reference token. `resourceType` and `structureType` both identify the data structure, but the R6 type is no longer limited to a primitive FHIR resource code.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a central content-model replacement. R4 instance declarations using `resourceId`, `resourceType`, or `name` are not valid R6, and R6 requires a `title`. R6 can also describe non-FHIR structures and example content references that R4 has no place to store.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrect instance-key migration can break operation request/response links and make scenario diagrams misleading.

justification.inferredGoal: Generalize scenario instances beyond FHIR resources and align instance references on stable keys.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `resourceId`, `resourceType`, and `name` for FHIR-resource instances while adding optional generalized structure fields for non-FHIR examples.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal is more than a cosmetic rename: the new model can describe non-FHIR structures, profiles, versions, and example content references. A less-breaking design could preserve many R4 instances, but it would either keep misleading FHIR-resource-specific fields in a generalized resource or support duplicate fields for the same instance identity and structure type. Those are material validation and interoperability tradeoffs, so the breaking remodel is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial alternative would keep `resourceId` as the instance key and `resourceType` as a shorthand for FHIR resource instances, add `structureType`/`structureVersion`/`structureProfile[x]`/`content` for richer cases, and make display `title` optional or warning-enforced. This preserves most old FHIR-resource scenarios but does not provide one clean representation for all instances; validators would need rules to reconcile or forbid conflicting `resourceType` and `structureType` values.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Covers common R4 FHIR-resource instances, but creates overlapping `resourceType`/`structureType` representations and leaves FHIR-specific names in a generalized model.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `instance.resourceType` as 1..1 code with required resource-types binding.
R6 defines `instance.structureType` as 1..1 Coding with extensible examplescenario-instance-type binding.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example uses a likely Coding for a FHIR resource type. Verify the preferred R6 coding system and display rules before production use.

findings.narrativeMd: The instance model changed from a FHIR-resource-specific shape to a generalized keyed data-structure shape. This affects almost every ExampleScenario that declares exchanged examples, because the mandatory R4 fields are gone and the mandatory R6 fields are different.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances with `instance.resourceId`, `instance.resourceType`, or `instance.name` are invalid against the R6 StructureDefinition. R6 instances using non-FHIR `structureType`, `structureVersion`, `structureProfile[x]`, or `content` cannot be faithfully represented in R4 without extensions or external metadata.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map `resourceId` to `key`. Convert `resourceType` into a `Coding` for `structureType`. Populate `title` from R4 `name` when present, otherwise choose a deterministic title and review. Preserve R6-only structure/profile/content metadata in extensions or a sidecar if R6-to-R4 round-trip matters.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The generalization is understandable because examples can now represent FHIR and non-FHIR structures. A less breaking alternative would have kept R4 FHIR-specific fields as aliases, but that would create ambiguous duplicate state.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The R6 instance type ValueSet includes R4/R6 resource-types and an external HL7 v2 table by composition; not all expansions were locally available.

findings.title: Instance version and contained-instance references were renamed and retitled

oldState.summary: R4 version used `versionId` 1..1 and `description` 1..1; contained instances used `resourceId` and optional `versionId`.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 required a version id and description for each instance version and referenced contained instances by resource id/version id strings.

newState.summary: R6 version uses `key` 1..1 and `title` 1..1, makes description optional, and contained instances use `instanceReference`/`versionReference`.

constraints.human: InstanceReference must be a key of an instance defined in the ExampleScenario
versionReference must be specified if the referenced instance defines versions
versionReference must be a key of a version within the instance pointed to by instanceReference

newState.narrativeMd: R6 makes version and contained-instance references part of the same key-based model used for actors and instances.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The old and new fields share the same containment positions and internal-reference semantics, but the R6 names and required display title are different.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances using `versionId`, contained `resourceId`, or contained `versionId` will not validate in R6. R6 also requires a version `title`, while R4 required `description`; neither direction has a perfectly lossless automatic mapping for all data.

justification.inferredGoal: Make version and contained-instance references align with the R6 key/title model and enforce referential integrity.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `versionId`, `containedInstance.resourceId`, and `containedInstance.versionId`, and define the new key/reference invariants over those existing fields.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of key-based version and contained-instance reference integrity is reasonable. The element-name break is probably avoidable because R4 already had mandatory identifiers and reference strings in the relevant locations; R6 could have clarified those fields and enforced resolvability without renaming them or requiring a new version `title` in the base model.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking R6 design could keep `version.versionId` as the version key and keep contained-instance `resourceId`/`versionId` as references, with invariants requiring them to resolve to declared instance/version identifiers. Version display titles could be optional, warning-level, or profile-required. The main cost is living with names that no longer align with the rest of the R6 `key`/`reference` vocabulary; accepting both old and new names would be worse because duplicate same-resource representations could persist indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoids wire-format breakage but retains older names that are less consistent with the R6 key/reference vocabulary and may be awkward for non-resource instances.

evidence.detail: R6 defines containedInstance.instanceReference as 1..1 string and constrains it to refer to an instance key.

findings.narrativeMd: The same key/title remodeling applies below `instance.version` and `instance.containedInstance`. This is especially important because operation request/response uses the contained-instance backbone by content reference, so old request/response references inherit the renamed child fields.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 `versionId`, `containedInstance.resourceId`, and `containedInstance.versionId` are not valid R6 properties. R6 `version.title` is mandatory, while R4 version descriptions were mandatory. R6 validators also enforce that contained instance references resolve to defined instance and version keys.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Copy version `versionId` to `version.key`; choose `version.title` from an existing display label, the old version id, or a curated title; preserve R4 `description` in R6 `description`. Rename contained instance `resourceId` to `instanceReference` and `versionId` to `versionReference`, then run reference-integrity validation across the whole resource.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The new names are consistent with the R6 key model, but a compatibility phase with old names would have avoided hard instance rejection. Because the new invariants depend on the new names, a permanent dual model would be costly.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Check examples where R4 `version.description` carried the only human-readable label. Mapping that text into R6 `title` may be too verbose, but using the old id may lose display semantics.

findings.title: Operation number/name/type were replaced by step number, required operation title, and Coding type

oldState.summary: R4 operation had mandatory `number`, optional `name`, and optional string `type`.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 placed the sequence number inside `operation.number`; the human-friendly name was optional, and operation type was an unconstrained string.

newState.summary: R6 moves the sequence number to `process.step.number`, requires `operation.title`, and changes `operation.type` to Coding.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 treats the operation title as required display text and standardizes operation type with a Coding drawn from RESTful interaction codes when applicable.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The sequence number concept moved from operation to step. The display label concept moved from optional `name` to mandatory `title`; `type` remains same path but changed representation.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 operation `number` and `name` are removed, R6 `operation.title` is required, and `operation.type` changes JSON shape from primitive string to object Coding. This breaks strict parsers, generated classes, serializers, templates, and code that treats operation type as a plain string.

justification.inferredGoal: Separate step sequence numbering from operation display labels and standardize operation kinds.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep old operation `number`, `name`, and string `type` while adding step-level numbering and an optional structured Coding for standardized operation kinds.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Separating step numbering from operation display text and standardizing operation type as a Coding are reasonable R6 goals. A compatibility design could cover common R4 instances, but it would materially complicate the model because operation numbers and step numbers could conflict, operation `name` and `title` could diverge, and arbitrary R4 type strings cannot always be represented as standard codings. Given those tradeoffs, the breaking design is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial alternative would retain `operation.number` as a deprecated alias for `step.number` on operation steps, retain `operation.name` as a display label, and add a separate optional Coding field or choice for standardized operation types. This is less breaking for direct R4 content, but it creates duplicate representations and ambiguous precedence rules; it also does not fully solve arbitrary R4 string types that have no suitable R6 operation code.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves many old operation steps, but duplicates numbering/type concepts and forces validators to reconcile arbitrary strings with coded operation semantics.

evidence.detail: R4 defines operation.type as 0..1 string with no binding.
R6 defines operation.type as 0..1 Coding with extensible examplescenario-operation-codes binding.

findings.narrativeMd: Operation rendering and typing changed substantially. The old mandatory operation number no longer exists at the operation level, while R6 requires a title and represents the type as a Coding. This is both a validation break and a codegen/runtime break.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: A direct R4 instance with `operation.number`, `operation.name`, or primitive string `operation.type` is not R6-valid. R6-to-R4 conversion can flatten some Coding values to strings, but system/display/version information is lost, and R6 `operation.title` must be mapped back to R4's optional `name` if desired.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Move old `operation.number` to `process.step.number`. Map old `operation.name` to `operation.title`; if absent, derive a title from the old type, number, or business description and flag for review. Convert known CRUD/REST strings to Coding values using `http://hl7.org/fhir/restful-interaction` where appropriate.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The structured Coding and separate step number are useful, but the same goal could have been introduced with additional optional fields while retaining old ones temporarily. The stricter R6 model reduces ambiguity for rendering but requires non-trivial migration.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Do not blindly map every R4 operation type string to a RESTful interaction code; R4 allowed arbitrary strings.

findings.title: Workflow nesting moved from root workflow to step.workflow and nested process cardinality narrowed

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 allowed multiple root nested workflows and multiple nested subprocesses within a step.

newState.summary: R6 removes root workflow, adds `process.step.workflow` 0..1, and narrows `process.step.process` to 0..1.

constraints.expression: (process.exists() implies workflow.empty() and operation.empty()) and (workflow.exists() implies operation.empty())
constraints.human: Can have a process, a workflow, one or more operations or none of these, but cannot have a combination

newState.narrativeMd: R6 associates external workflow references with a specific step and allows only one nested process or workflow per step, mutually exclusive with operation.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The canonical self-reference target is preserved, but the location changes from a root-level list to a step-level field. This is a move plus a cardinality/context change, not a simple rename.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances with root `workflow` are not valid R6 because the element no longer exists. R4 instances with multiple `process.step.process` entries in one step exceed the R6 max of 1. R6 step-scoped workflow references cannot be represented as R4 root workflows without losing step context.

justification.inferredGoal: Model workflow references as specific step actions rather than resource-level unrelated links.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep root `workflow` and repeating nested `process` during a transition while adding step-scoped `workflow` for new content.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of saying which step invokes a workflow, and of constraining a step to one process/workflow/operation action, is semantically stronger than the R4 shape. A less-breaking design exists for common old instances, but it is incomplete: root workflows lack step context, and allowing repeated nested processes preserves the ambiguity R6 appears to be removing. The break is therefore probably justified if the one-action, step-scoped model is a core goal.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial alternative would keep `ExampleScenario.workflow` as deprecated root metadata and keep `process.step.process` repeating, while adding `process.step.workflow` for precise new content. That would allow R4 root workflows and multi-process steps to validate, but consumers would need precedence and consistency rules when both root and step workflow links are present, and R6 tooling could not rely on a single action per step.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old workflow links and multi-process steps, but allows ambiguous root-vs-step workflow placement and weakens the one-action-per-step model.

evidence.detail: R4 defines root workflow as 0..* canonical targeting ExampleScenario.
R6 defines step.workflow as 0..1 canonical targeting ExampleScenario.
R4 allows multiple nested processes per step.
R6 allows only one nested process per step.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 fragment carries step context that the R4 root `workflow` list cannot preserve without an extension or convention.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 changes workflow nesting from a root-level list to a step-level action and narrows nested subprocess cardinality. This affects both validation and the meaning of nested scenarios: R6 can say exactly which step invokes another workflow, while R4 could only list related workflows at the resource root.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 root `workflow` is old-valid/new-invalid. Multiple nested `process.step.process` repetitions in R4 are also invalid in R6. R6 step-level `workflow` is not cleanly representable in R4 because moving it to the root loses where it happened.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4 root workflows, identify the step that should invoke each referenced workflow and move the canonical to `process.step.workflow`. If no step context can be inferred, manual review or an extension is needed. Split R4 steps with multiple nested processes into multiple R6 steps or choose a single nested process per step.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The step-scoped model is semantically stronger, but removal of the root list was avoidable by keeping it as deprecated metadata. The tradeoff is that keeping both would allow inconsistent root and step workflow references.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: This finding combines an element move and a cardinality narrowing because both affect nested workflow/subprocess migration.

findings.title: R6 adds local invariants for completeness, uniqueness, mutual exclusion, and internal references

oldState.summary: R4 had no comparable local error invariants beyond the name warning and base constraints.

constraints.human: Name should be usable as an identifier for the module by machine processing applications such as code generation

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 primarily relied on cardinalities and type/binding rules for local ExampleScenario validation.

newState.summary: R6 adds many local `exs-*` error and warning constraints.

constraints.human: Must have actors if status is active or required
Must have processes if status is active or required
Processes must have steps if ExampleScenario status is active or required
InstanceReference must be a key of an instance defined in the ExampleScenario
If specified, initiator must be a key of an actor within the ExampleScenario
If specified, receiver must be a key of an actor within the ExampleScenario

constraints.expression: (process.exists() implies workflow.empty() and operation.empty()) and (workflow.exists() implies operation.empty())
constraints.human: Can have a process, a workflow, one or more operations or none of these, but cannot have a combination
actor SHALL have either a type or a definition but not both

newState.narrativeMd: R6 makes internal consistency part of base validation: active/retired scenarios need actors and processes, keys and titles must be unique in several scopes, references must resolve, and mutually exclusive child choices are enforced.

facts.newValue: active/retired require actors, processes, and process steps
actor, instance, version, process title, and alternative title uniqueness constraints
contained instance references and operation initiator/receiver references must resolve

impact.impactRationaleMd: Some R4-valid resources can become R6-invalid even after field renames. For example, an active R4 ExampleScenario with no actors or no processes was structurally valid in R4 but fails R6 `exs-3`/`exs-4`. Duplicated keys or dangling initiator/receiver/resource references also become validation errors.

justification.inferredGoal: Ensure ExampleScenario instances are complete enough to render and internally consistent enough to be computable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Introduce the new integrity checks as warnings or profile rules before making them base error constraints.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The new constraints serve a real computability and rendering goal: active scenarios need usable content, keys should be unique, and internal references should resolve. A warning-first or profile-only path would be less breaking, but it would not give base R6 consumers the same validation guarantees. Because those guarantees are central to a computable ExampleScenario model, the hard-error approach is probably justified despite migration cost.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial alternative would downgrade some `exs-*` constraints to warning severity for one release, or place them in profiles for published/active scenarios. That preserves more R4-derived data during migration, but it is incomplete for the R6 base goal because validators and renderers would still have to handle dangling references, duplicate keys, and active scenarios without actors or processes.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Reduces migration rejection but lets base R6 instances remain incomplete, internally inconsistent, or harder for tooling to render reliably.

evidence.detail: R4 local ExampleScenario constraints include only the `esc-0` name warning; the many `exs-*` error constraints are absent.
R6 adds root constraints requiring actors/processes for active or retired scenarios and uniqueness of actor/instance/process title fields.
R6 requires contained-instance references to point to declared instance/version keys.
R6 requires initiator and receiver to resolve to actor keys or `OTHER`.

examples.examplesMd: A minimal active R4 scenario could omit `actor` and `process`; R6 `exs-3` and `exs-4` reject that combination. Real failures can also arise from duplicate titles/keys or unresolved references after migration.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds a local validation layer that turns previously informal modeling expectations into base errors. These constraints are not just documentation: FHIRPath-capable validators can reject resources based on completeness, uniqueness, mutual exclusion, and internal reference resolution.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: The validation mechanism is direct constraint evaluation. Old-valid/new-invalid cases include active or retired scenarios without actors/processes, processes without steps, duplicate keys/titles, contained-instance references that do not resolve to instance/version keys, and operations whose initiator or receiver is not an actor key or `OTHER`.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: After structural transformation, run an R6 validator and specifically test the `exs-*` invariants. Generate stable unique keys, de-duplicate or disambiguate titles, add missing actors/processes for active or retired scenarios, and resolve initiator/receiver/request/response references. Do not assume a syntactic field rename is sufficient.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The constraints are likely justified for computability and rendering. A warning-first migration path would have been less breaking but would allow invalid diagrams and dangling references in base R6 instances.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The constraint text contains wording such as 'active or required' where the FHIRPath uses `active` or `retired`; rely on the expression for validation mechanics.

findings.title: R6 adds optional content that is not losslessly representable in R4

oldState.summary: R4 lacks root `title`, `description`, `versionAlgorithm[x]`, `copyrightLabel`, actor definitions, instance content/profile metadata, and step-scoped workflow.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 can represent many basic scenario concepts, but it has no native elements for several R6 additions.

newState.summary: R6 adds several optional fields across the root and backbone structures.
newState.narrativeMd: New optional R6 content includes root `title`, root `description`, `versionAlgorithm[x]`, `copyrightLabel`, `actor.definition`, `instance.structureVersion`, `instance.structureProfile[x]`, `instance.content`, `instance.version.content`, `process.step.number`, and `process.step.workflow`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: These are additive R6 elements with no same-path R4 element and no unambiguous R4 target, except for partial lossy mapping into narrative or extensions.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Additive R6 fields do not make R4 instances invalid in R6, but they create loss on downgrade or round-trip. Some fields, such as `actor.definition` and `instance.content`, carry computable links that cannot be preserved in R4 without extensions.

justification.inferredGoal: Add richer metadata, formal actor links, example content references, and version comparison support.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking R6 base alternative is needed because these are additive optional R6 fields, not R4-to-R6 instance-breaking constraints.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: This finding is a reverse-direction representability issue. Adding optional R6 metadata, actor definitions, profile/content references, and step-scoped workflow content does not make R4-valid instances invalid in R6. The additions are therefore justified as R6 capabilities; the compatibility concern is only that plain R4 cannot natively carry them on downgrade.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Backward-compatible alternative analysis is not applicable under the calibration rules because this is additive optional R6 content and a pure R6-to-R4 downgrade/round-trip concern. Extensions, sidecar storage, or lossy downgrade policies may preserve data for R4 systems, but they are mitigations and should not be counted as a less-breaking base R6 design.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6-to-R4 extensions or sidecar metadata can mitigate downgrade loss, but those are conversion strategies rather than base R6 compatibility alternatives.

evidence.detail: R6 adds versionAlgorithm[x] as 0..1 string or Coding.

examples.examplesMd: A downgrade could copy root `title` into R4 `name` only if it is machine-friendly, but that changes semantics and loses the distinction between computer name and human title.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds richer optional content throughout the resource. These additions are not R4-to-R6 breaking, but they matter for systems that must downgrade R6 content or maintain one model that writes both versions.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R6 instances using these new fields are valid R6 but not directly representable as conformant R4 base elements. A strict R4 parser will reject them if copied as ordinary properties. Lossless round-trip requires extensions, sidecar storage, or version-aware persistence.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R6-to-R4, define an explicit data retention policy. Preserve important R6-only fields in extensions using documented URLs, store them outside the R4 instance, or accept lossy downgrade. Test downgrade/upgrade round-trips for title/name, actor.definition, structureProfile, content references, and workflow placement.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The additions are reasonable R6 features. Since R4 cannot be changed, backward compatibility depends on cross-version extension conventions rather than a base artifact alternative.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Some R6-only additions overlap with earlier structural findings; this finding captures the reverse-direction round-trip risk across all additive fields.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, abstract flag, derivation, and baseDefinition remain `ExampleScenario` as a concrete `DomainResource` specialization. R6 is not a rename, split, merge, or removal.

The self-reference canonical target remains `http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/ExampleScenario` where present, but the workflow element moved from root to step context and is covered as a finding. New `actor.definition` and content `Reference` elements are additive R6-only risks covered separately.
No local fixed value, pattern, or default value changes were identified on ExampleScenario elements.
No local maxLength, minValue, maxValue, or regex value-limit changes were found beyond the local constraints reported separately.
The local `status` modifier flag remains true. Inherited `modifierExtension` flag/summary details are out of scope for this artifact.
No local slicing discriminators or slice rules were identified in either R4 or R6 ExampleScenario.

Existing local summary flags such as `url`, `identifier`, `version`, `name`, `status`, and `process.title` are stable. Some R6-added root metadata fields are summary elements, but those are additive and covered under R6-only representability.

No XML/JSON representation-format change independent of element renames/type changes was found. Serialization impact is driven by the local element removals, new required fields, and primitive-to-Coding conversion reported in findings.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 StructureDefinition status is active instead of draft
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: This is metadata about the artifact definition, not an instance element cardinality or type change. It does not make R4 instances invalid by itself.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Treat the R6 resource as more mature/official than the R4 draft artifact when prioritizing migration work.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Jurisdiction binding canonical moved to terminology.hl7.org
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The binding strength remains extensible and the element type/cardinality are unchanged. The change is likely a canonical relocation of the common jurisdiction value set rather than a direct instance-breaking constraint.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Terminology clients that key on value set URL should recognize that R4 used `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/jurisdiction` while R6 uses `http://terminology.hl7.org/ValueSet/jurisdiction`. A terminology expansion would improve confidence.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Instance version description minimum decreased from 1 to 0
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The direction is a loosening for R4-to-R6 validation: R4 instances with descriptions still satisfy the R6 optional description rule.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: For R6-to-R4 downgrade, an R6 version without `description` cannot satisfy R4's mandatory `version.description` unless a value is generated. The broader version remodel is covered in the main findings.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: R6 `ExampleScenario.actor.definition` can reference `ActorDefinition`, and actor type terminology is aligned to ActorDefinition. Analyze ActorDefinition separately for its own R4/R6 migration implications.

Inherited changes such as `language` binding strengthening, modifierExtension summary behavior, and base element constraint wording are intentionally excluded here and should be owned by base artifact reports.
Automated migration needs explicit terminology mappings/expansions for actor type, instance structure type, operation Coding, and jurisdiction canonical changes.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4-to-R6 diff or ballot change note was available in the local inputs. Structural evidence is strong, but design intent and backward-compatible alternative assessment are partly inferred.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review the official FHIR change log, ballot notes, or generated diff pages for ExampleScenario.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The analysis inspected local ValueSet compose and local CodeSystems where available, but did not use a terminology server to expand every R4/R6 value set. The R6 jurisdiction ValueSet is referenced from terminology.hl7.org and was not present as a local package file.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Run terminology expansions for the relevant R4 and R6 value sets and obtain official ConceptMaps if available.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No corpus of real-world R4 ExampleScenario instances was validated. Prevalence estimates are based on the structure model and likely use patterns rather than measured instance frequency.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Validate representative R4 ExampleScenario examples against R4, transform them, and validate against R6 to quantify actual failure rates.
